_README: PIXELTOSSA character design 'natural': a working performer in a black tailcoat and gold waistcoat - realistic adult proportions
GENERATED by PixelLab on the locked palette, then fitted by scripts/fit_char_design.py.
Selected on the F9 panel (THE LOOK > The performer) or with --variant character:natural.
THE FIGURE HAS NO ARMS, and that is the point. Hand positions are the MECHANIC -
outer_pos and inner_pos are where a catch and a throw happen and every pattern's
choreography is written in them - so they do not move for a costume. But the arms are
not art at all: draw_arm solves a two-bone IK to wherever the hand is THIS frame. A
painted-on arm would freeze, and the juggler would catch with his elbows. So the arms
are cut off here and the game draws them, in this design's own sleeve colour, from
the shoulder point in _FIGURE to the hands it already had.
That is also how the arms got SHORTER without touching the mechanic: a design with
wider shoulders makes the same hand position a shorter reach.
_FIGURE is landmark geometry as fractions of the sprite's OWN ink height. The game
reads the height back off the texture and lays the figure out from that, so the art
is drawn at exactly ART_PIXEL screen pixels per art pixel and is never resampled.
